---
title: "References"
description: "Works the joshpy documentation draws on, grouped by page"
---

joshpy implements no statistics of its own. Optimization and inference come from
established packages maintained by others, and the docs describe them in the
terms of the papers below. Each page lists the works it cites at its end. This
page collects them, grouped by page.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Adding a reference

Add the BibTeX entry to `docs/references.bib`, cite it in a page with `[@key]`,
and list it below under that page's heading. Quarto formats the citation and
adds the entry to the page's own reference list.
:::

## Inference: overview

[Page](inference/index.qmd)

- @hartig2011: the framework the Inference pages follow for stochastic
  ecological simulation models: aggregation into summary statistics, likelihood
  approximation, and sampling, with four options for the approximation.
- @cranmer2020: the wider field of simulation-based inference, including
  amortized neural estimators.
- @boelts2025: the sbi package that `SbiStrategy` runs.
- @toni2009 and @beaumont2009: sequential Monte Carlo ABC and its importance
  weights, as implemented in sbi.
- @wood2010: synthetic likelihood, a parametric likelihood approximation.
- @wilkinson2013: the tolerance read as an explicit model-error term.

## Inference: ForeverTree case study

[Page](inference/forevertree.qmd)

- @hartig2011: aggregation into summary statistics, sufficiency, and scaling;
  why a stochastic simulator's likelihood has to be approximated, and how the
  approximation works at a single parameter value.
- @zurell2010: the virtual ecologist approach, simulating the observer (here, the
  survey's measurement error) along with the system.
- @wilkinson2013: the alternative to simulating the survey, a tolerance sized to
  the observation error.
- @csillery2012: the reference table of parameters and statistics.
- @grimm2005: pattern-oriented modelling, whose patterns are summary statistics.
- @joyce2008, @fearnhead2012 and @blum2013: choosing or constructing summary
  statistics automatically.
- @beaumont2002: scaling each statistic by its spread across simulations.
- @wood2010: synthetic likelihood, the parametric alternative to ABC's match
  counting.

## Inference: SMC-ABC on a simulated survey

[Page](inference/smc-abc.qmd)

- @hartig2011: the nonparametric likelihood approximation, the tolerance as
  approximation error, and testing sufficiency on artificial data.
- @toni2009 and @beaumont2009: sequential Monte Carlo ABC and its importance
  weights.
- @cranmer2020: the tolerance as approximation error, and neural estimators
  beyond a handful of statistics.
- @wilkinson2013: the tolerance read as an unsimulated observation error.
- @beven2006: equifinality, parameter sets that reproduce the data equally
  well.
- @grimm2005: the posterior predictive check as a held-out pattern.
- @talts2018 and @csillery2012: the coverage check over held-out simulations.
- @beaumont2002: regression adjustment of accepted parameters.

## Inference: A model with births and deaths

[Page](inference/fire-model.qmd)

- @zurell2010: the virtual ecologist: the survey, and the juveniles it misses,
  simulated with the system.
- @hartig2011: summary statistics, and testing their sufficiency on simulated
  data.
- @joyce2008: approximate sufficiency: adding statistics that leave the
  posterior unchanged.

## Inference: What would it take?

[Page](inference/rejection-filter.qmd)

- @hartig2011: the rejection filter, option (d) of the likelihood
  approximation: keep the parameter sets whose output meets stated criteria.
- @grimm2005: pattern-oriented modelling, which filters parameter sets by
  patterns observed in the field.
- @hanley1983: the rule of three, a 95% upper bound of about $3/n$ on a
  probability when none of $n$ draws passes.

## Inference: Posterior probability of the target

[Page](inference/posterior-property.qmd)

- @hanley1983: the rule of three, applied to the posterior's effective sample
  size.

## Adaptive Parameter Optimization

[Tutorial](tutorials/adaptive-sweep.qmd)

- @akiba2019: Optuna, the framework behind `OptunaStrategy`.
- @bergstra2011: the tree-structured Parzen estimator (TPE), the sampler the
  tutorial uses.
